solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent companion — a politician and I will get on

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend, a member of parliament and the speaker expect to get along famously.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, champion is a dated British word for first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: US television network includes odd bits

indicators.note: one network's name holds the other word within it

parts.note: CBS is an American broadcaster
rum is a British word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: An American broadcaster's schedule contains some peculiar fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs are small fragments, a synonym for scraps or bits of something.

clue.text: Promise made by fool on northern river

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other, so it comes first

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A pledge given by an idiot standing beside a river up north.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to give them a pledge or guarantee, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Solid figure of knight turning up to be received by premier

indicators.note: the prime minister's letters take the reversed title into their middle

parts.note: PM is short for prime minister

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A knight is shown in to meet the prime minister, cutting a solid figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a prism is a solid with two identical parallel faces joined by parallelograms.

clue.text: Open with a sign that something's wrong — stress too much

parts.note: overt means done openly, not hidden
a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Beginning with a warning signal, someone puts too much strain on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax is to strain or burden beyond reasonable limits, i.e. overstress.

clue.text: Sound of drunken sailor in unruly incident at the controls

indicators.note: the letters are what a phrase sounds like when spoken

parts.note: high means intoxicated and a jack is a sailor

explanation.surface: A tipsy seaman is heard causing chaos on the flight deck.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH JACK, a drunk sailor, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijack is the seizing of a vehicle or aircraft by force, taking over its controls.

clue.text: Tumbler's content ______, that's clear!

parts.note: a tumbler's contents are in glass, and the word itself names a clear gelatin or mica

explanation.surface: A drinker states the obvious about what is in a beaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a transparent gelatin from fish bladders, and also a name for clear mica sheets.

clue.text: Spanning entrance to theatre is a charmingly old-fashioned etching

indicators.note: the word for old-fashioned stretches across the letter from the theatre

parts.note: quaint means attractively old-world

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An antique print stretches over the doorway of a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatint is an etching method using acid on resin to give tonal effects like watercolour.

clue.text: Dan keeps crashing — protection for joints needed

indicators.note: the letters collide and break into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy cyclist named Dan keeps falling, so he needs padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneepads are padded guards strapped over the knee, a joint at risk in a fall.

clue.text: A Parisian suit's beginning to get greasy — so clean

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: oiled means covered in oil

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's outfit is starting to look oily, though it is still spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsoiled means not dirtied, i.e. spotless or clean.

clue.text: Very little time for measuring the pulse?

definitions.meaning: a pulse is counted in beats per sixty seconds

explanation.surface: A nurse needs only a moment to take a pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced differently, the word means tiny, and also sixty seconds, the span used for counting a heart rate.

clue.text: Supplicate quietly — bit of hope follows

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
a ray of hope is a glimmer

explanation.surface: Someone begs softly when a glimmer of hope appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplicate is to ask humbly, as a petitioner does in prayer.

clue.text: One can tell what pressure we are under

definitions.text: One can tell what pressure we are under

parts.words: One can tell what pressure we are under
parts.note: sounds like a confidant who reads stress, but means the air pressure above us

explanation.surface: A sympathetic friend senses how stressed everybody is.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, the weight of air we live beneath.

clue.text: Rise from place say, having been knocked over

indicators.note: the pieces are turned right round, so read backwards

parts.note: to put is to place
eg means for example

explanation.surface: A man gets to his feet after being bowled over.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up is to rise from sitting or lying, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: I become cross, having come to destroy beast

indicators.note: the second word is wiped out of the first

parts.note: an X is a cross

explanation.surface: Someone grows angry and arrives intent on killing an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Ban the heartless group trafficking?

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit

indicators.note: the middle of the word is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: a ring is a gang or circle of people

explanation.surface: A call to outlaw a cruel gang involved in smuggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartering is trading goods, and trafficking can mean dealing or trading in general.

clue.text: Longed to be scholarly, given new head

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: learned means erudite

explanation.surface: Someone wished to be an academic, after a change at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned is to have ached or pined for something.

clue.text: Trouble taken initially to store the Spanish litres — in this cupboard?

indicators.note: the word for trouble holds the other letters inside

parts.note: care means trouble or pains
el is Spanish for the
l is the symbol for litres

indicators.note: the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Bottles of Spanish wine, carefully counted, are kept in a sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard for holding bottles of wine.

clue.text: Style of singing that could convey noble act

indicators.note: the letters may be carried into another order

explanation.surface: A form of vocal music might express a heroic deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel canto is the lyrical Italian operatic vocal style of the 18th and 19th centuries.

clue.text: One of two arches either side of a bridge

definitions.text: One of two arches either side of a bridge

parts.words: One of two arches either side of a bridge
parts.note: suggests a river crossing, but the bridge is that of the nose

explanation.surface: A description of a stone river crossing with paired arches.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairy ridges over the eyes arch on either side of the bridge of the nose.

clue.text: Person full of humour and energy gets remuneration

parts.note: a wag is a joker
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lively joker gets paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is regular pay for work, a synonym of remuneration.

clue.text: Enthusiasm brings prizes, though with many missing out

indicators.note: most letters are dropped, leaving a run that spans the two words

explanation.surface: Keen people win prizes, yet many miss out.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest means keen enjoyment or gusto, a synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Re-establishment of Nazi set is most bizarre

indicators.note: the letters are set up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Bringing back a fascist clique would be the maddest idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaniest is the superlative of zany, meaning comically odd.

clue.text: Hunger in the morning when there's possible food around?

indicators.note: the word for food sits round the other letters

parts.note: fish is one example of food
am means before noon

explanation.surface: Feeling peckish at breakfast when there might be kippers on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to starve or make very hungry; as a verb it parallels hunger.

clue.text: Ten roughly accommodated in apartment? Only five here

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are housed within the flat

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat

indicators.note: loosely arranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Ten people crammed into a flat, though only five belong.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a set or group of five things.

clue.text: Fortune no end about to be made — filthy money

indicators.note: the final letter is cut off

parts.note: luck means fortune
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Making a fortune endlessly is all about dirty cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money regarded as sordid, as in the phrase 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Good to join mate visiting a nice rickety bar

indicators.note: the friend goes into the scrambled letters
shaky, so the letters are unsettled

parts.note: pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend drops into a shabby but pleasant pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PAL goes into INACE, the anagram of A NICE from 'rickety'. A GIN PALACE is a showy Victorian British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a gaudy Victorian pub, so it is a kind of bar.

clue.text: After start of argument fight roughly

indicators.note: the fight comes after the opening letter
the first letter of the word after

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match

explanation.surface: Following an opening row, people come to blows more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: About means approximately, a synonym of roughly.

clue.text: Crime writer managed to get ink flowing

parts.note: ran means ran a business, managed it

indicators.note: the letters run freely into a new order

explanation.surface: An author of detective fiction gets the pen going.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Rankin is a Scottish author famous for his Inspector Rebus crime novels.

clue.text: New poet isn't one to help friends or relations

definitions.text: one to help friends or relations

indicators.note: made new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh poet who refuses to favour his circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nepotist favours family or friends, especially in giving jobs.

clue.text: Depression over with first husband out of the way

indicators.note: something moved out of the way is cleared off, so this letter is taken out of the word for over

parts.note: through means finished, over

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first H, the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Getting over one's sadness after the first husband has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a low point or hollow, so a depression in land or the economy.

clue.text: Like yarn running through a book?

definitions.text: Like yarn running through a book?

parts.words: Like yarn running through a book?
parts.note: yarn suggests a story told through a novel, but it is thread sewing the pages

explanation.surface: A story that unfolds across a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Book pages bound with thread are sewn, so the binding yarn passes through them.
